blocks.text: וְעִשָּׂרוֹן אֶחָד לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד לְשִׁבְעַת הַכְּבָשִׂים׃ וּשְׂעִיר־עִזִּים אֶחָד חַטָּאת לְכַפֵּר עֲלֵיכֶם׃ מִלְּבַד עֹלַת הַחֹדֶשׁ וּמִנְחָתָהּ וְעֹלַת הַתָּמִיד וּמִנְחָתָהּ וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ אִשֶּׁה לַיהוָה׃
uncertainties: Te'amim are clearly printed on this text but are left out here; only consonants, niqqud, dagesh, maqaf and sof pasuq are transcribed. See notes.
וּשְׂעִיר־ is split across a line break as וּשְׂעִיר־ / עִזִּים; it is joined at the maqaf.
Spellings as printed: עֹלַת (twice) and הַחֹדֶשׁ are defective; עִשָּׂרוֹן and נִיחֹחַ are as shown.
ליהוה is printed with the full Tetragrammaton, not the יְיָ abbreviation, and is pointed לַיהוָה.

blocks.text: מי שברך. ומגביהין וגוללין. כשמגביהין הס״ת מביטין נגד הכתב של ס״ת ואומרין:
uncertainties: Printed in Rashi script. The word מי is in a heavier type.
The punctuation between מי שברך and ומגביהין is read as a period.

blocks.text: וְזֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אֲשֶׁר־שָׂם מֹשֶׁה לִפְנֵי בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל־פִּי יְיָ בְּיַד־מֹשֶׁה׃ עֵץ־חַיִּים הִיא לַמַּחֲזִיקִים בָּהּ וְתוֹמְכֶיהָ מְאֻשָּׁר׃ דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי־נֹעַם וְכָל־נְתִיבֹתֶיהָ שָׁלוֹם׃ אֹרֶךְ יָמִים בִּימִינָהּ בִּשְׂמֹאלָהּ עֹשֶׁר וְכָבוֹד׃ יְיָ חָפֵץ לְמַעַן צִדְקוֹ יַגְדִּיל תּוֹרָה וְיַאְדִּיר׃
uncertainties: וְכָל־ is split across a line break as וְכָל־ / נְתִיבֹתֶיהָ; it is joined at the maqaf.
וְתוֹמְכֶיהָ looks plene (with holam-vav), but the scan is unclear.
נְתִיבֹתֶיהָ looks defective (no vav), but the scan is unclear.
The divine name is printed as יְיָ.

blocks.text: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם אֲשֶׁר בָּחַר בִּנְבִיאִים טוֹבִים וְרָצָה בְדִבְרֵיהֶם הַנֶּאֱמָרִים בֶּאֱמֶת בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְיָ הַבּוֹחֵר בַּתּוֹרָה וּבְמֹשֶׁה עַבְדּוֹ וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵל עַמּוֹ וּבִנְבִיאֵי הָאֱמֶת וָצֶדֶק׃

The meteg and accent-like strokes under הַנֶּאֱמָרִים and בֶּאֱמֶת are hard to tell apart.

blocks.text: וַיְהִי אִישׁ אֶחָד מִן־הָרָמָתַיִם צוֹפִים מֵהַר אֶפְרָיִם וּשְׁמוֹ אֶלְקָנָה בֶּן־יְרֹחָם בֶּן־אֱלִיהוּא בֶּן־תֹּחוּ בֶן־צוּף אֶפְרָתִי׃ וְלוֹ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים שֵׁם אַחַת חַנָּה וְשֵׁם הַשֵּׁנִית פְּנִנָּה וַיְהִי לִפְנִנָּה יְלָדִים וּלְחַנָּה אֵין יְלָדִים׃ וְעָלָה הָאִישׁ הַהוּא מֵעִירוֹ מִיָּמִים יָמִימָה לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺת וְלִזְבֹּחַ לַיהוָה צְבָאוֹת בְּשִׁלֹה וְשָׁם שְׁנֵי בְנֵי־עֵלִי
uncertainties: The page breaks in the middle of verse 3 after בְנֵי־עֵלִי, with no sof pasuq. The verse continues on the following scan.
Te'amim are printed but are left out here (see notes).
I can't tell whether בֶן־צוּף has a dagesh in the bet. It is given as בֶן, but the print may show בֶּן.
לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺת: the holam over the vav is hard to see, so the exact form of the vav may be wrong.
The divine name is printed in full as לַיהוָה, not as יְיָ.
There is a long stroke at the end of the line after לִפְנִנָּה. It could be an accent (pashta?) or a line filler, and is not transcribed.

for each of the seven lambs. And also one he-goat as a sin-offering to atone for you. Apart from the whole-offering of the new moon and its meal-offering and the regular whole-offering with its meal-offering and their drink-offerings according to their rule for a sweet savour, a fire offering to the Lord.

blocks.text: After the reading, the Torah scroll is lifted up and rolled together again. When the Torah scroll is being lifted up, one says:
וזאת

This is the Torah which Moses placed before the Children of Israel at the Lord's command through Moses. It is a tree of life for those who grasp it; and whoever supports it, is made happy. Its ways are pleasant and all its paths are peace. Length of days is in its right hand, in its left is wealth and honour. The Lord delights for the sake of His righteousness to magnify the Torah and to glorify it.
uncertainties: Line-break hyphens are joined: Chil-/dren → Children, right-/eousness → righteousness.

blocks.text: Blessing before the Haphtorah:
ברוך

Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the World, who has chosen worthy prophets and found pleasure in their words that are spoken in truth. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who has chosen the Torah and His servant Moses, His people Israel and prophets of truth and righteousness.
Haphtarah
uncertainties: The heading is spelled 'Haphtarah', but the running head and the rubric spell it 'Haphtorah'. Both are recorded as printed.

blocks.text: (1 Samuel, ch. 1—2 v. 10)
uncertainties: The digits are old-style figures; the '1' looks like a small-capital I.

blocks.text: ויהי

There was once a man from Romathaim-Tsofim, from the hill-country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah the son of Yeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Tsuf, an Efrathite. He had two wives; the name of one was Hannah and that of the other was Peninah; Peninah had children but Hannah had no children. This man used to go up from his town year by year to Shiloh in order to prostrate himself and to sacrifice before the Lord of Hosts. There were two sons of Eli, Hofni and Pinhas, priests to the Lord. On
uncertainties: The page ends mid-sentence with 'On'. The text continues on the next page.
The English page runs a little ahead of the Hebrew page: 'Hofni and Pinhas, priests to the Lord' finishes verse 3, while the Hebrew stops at בְנֵי־עֵלִי.

notes: The brief says this Torah and Haftarah text has no full cantillation. That does not match the scan: s174 clearly has te'amim on the Numbers 29 verses, the Haftarah blessing and 1 Samuel 1:1–3. Following the instruction not to supply signs from memory, and because I can't reliably tell te'amim from meteg in this scan, I left all te'amim out of the Hebrew text fields. These pages will need a separate accent pass if they are wanted.

Rare printed accents: (1) מִלְּבַד (Numbers 29:6) has a small circle accent, a telisha, printed above the end of the word (left side), which is the telisha qetanah position. Whether the printer meant telisha gedolah is uncertain. (2) וְשָׁם (1 Samuel 1:3) has a double-stroke accent above the shin, read as gershayim.
No marginal qere/ketiv notes are visible on either page.
No aliyah labels or chapter labels are printed on these pages, apart from the Haftarah citation 'בשמואל א׳ סמן א׳'.
The divine name is handled two ways: biblical verses use the full Tetragrammaton (לַיהוָה), while liturgical texts (וזאת התורה, the blessing) use יְיָ.

Where verses and paragraphs cross the page: Numbers 29:4 begins on the previous scan. 1 Samuel 1:3 continues past the end of both pages: the Hebrew stops after בְנֵי־עֵלִי, and the English stops after 'On', which belongs to verse 4.
I read the overlapping bands s174-band1 to band4, s175-band1 and s175-band3, plus both full pages. Lines repeated across the overlaps are included only once.
